sources.entry: GitAhead - A graphical Git client designed to help you understand and manage your source code history.

summary.one_liner: GitAhead is a graphical Git client for understanding and managing source code history, available as prebuilt binaries for Windows, Linux, and macOS or buildable from source.
summary.what_it_does: GitAhead is a desktop GUI for Git, built with C++ and Qt, aimed at helping users understand and manage their repository history. The README says it ships as a pre-built binary for Windows, Linux, and macOS, and can also be compiled from source using CMake. The build uses bundled submodules for libgit2 (the Git library) and cmark (Markdown parsing), with optional git for credential helpers and libssh2/OpenSSL for SSH support. The README does not describe specific UI features beyond the one-line description. The project is MIT licensed.
use_cases: browse and understand git commit history visually
manage a local git repository without the command line
build a Git GUI client from source
work with git repositories on Windows, Linux, or macOS
how_to_run: cd dep/openssl/openssl && ./config -fPIC && make  (Linux; README gives different Configure commands for Win and Mac)
notable: Pre-built binaries provided for Windows, Linux, and macOS
Bundled dependencies as git submodules (libgit2, cmark, libssh2, OpenSSL)
caveats: No longer under active development; only low-level maintenance and bug-fix releases are planned, with no new features
Building from source requires initializing submodules and building OpenSSL first, with platform-specific steps (Perl and NASM needed on Windows)
Qt 5.9 or newer must be installed or pointed to via CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH
